data.title: Use an agent-first control plane over existing services
data.context: The operator wants Telegram outcomes without manually coordinating several media applications.
data.decision: Keep existing services authoritative and build deterministic doctor, plan, apply, and verify operations over their APIs.
consequences: The first value slice is read-only diagnosis; a dashboard is not required.

data.title: Keep all deployment state outside Git
data.context: The repository is public while real stacks contain credentials, network identities, media history, and generated operational evidence.
data.decision: Track schemas and synthetic fixtures only; store secrets, inventories, plans, logs, databases, and caches in protected external runtime directories.
consequences: Public tests cannot depend on a live household stack.

data.title: Use local repository gates instead of GitHub Actions
data.context: The repository needs reproducible CI-equivalent validation without depending on hosted workflow execution.
data.decision: Make bash scripts/check.sh the canonical gate and require fresh-clone execution before releases.
consequences: Contributors run the same deterministic gate locally; hosted CI can be reconsidered only by explicit policy change.

data.title: Track only disclosure-passed public deliveries
data.context: The foundation review auto-generated a restricted delivery with scan_status blocked. Committing that artifact to a public repository contradicts the repository's public-data boundary even though the artifact contains no discovered secret.
data.decision: The public repository retains canonical task and JSONL evidence, but tracks generated delivery HTML only when disclosure.class is public and scan_status is passed.
consequences: Restricted, link-private, and scan-blocked delivery artifacts remain outside the current tracked tree.

data.title: Use a disposable isolated Compose lab
data.context: Service integration and mutation logic must be developed without exposing the WSL host, LAN, private media, or the real NUC.
data.decision: Run one Compose project per lab ID on a single internal bridge with isolated gateway mode, zero published host ports, external marked runtime state, and host-owned Docker authority.
consequences: Container-to-host, host-to-container, LAN, and internet reachability are negative gates; no runner or controller receives the Docker socket.

data.title: Use real services plus deterministic doubles
data.context: Fixtures alone cannot prove startup, authentication, official API behavior, path mappings, or upstream drift, while real services cannot reproduce every protocol fault deterministically.
data.decision: Use real pinned Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, qBittorrent, and Jellyfin containers for normal integration and repository-owned minimal doubles only for synthetic indexer behavior and deterministic protocol faults.
consequences: Every adapter has a fast fixture lane and a focused real-container lane; doubles contain only minimal synthetic data.

data.title: Run service API tests inside the isolated network
data.context: Publishing application APIs or calling container IPs from the WSL host would weaken the lab trust boundary and contradict the zero-port contract.
data.decision: The WSL host invokes one-shot lab-controller or arrctl-runner commands through Docker Compose; all application API traffic originates inside the isolated application network.
consequences: Host tests remain orchestration and contract tests; real-container integration and E2E commands execute in the controller image without debug ports or a second network.

data.title: Require lab proof before live stack promotion
data.context: The current CLI skeleton has no production-ready adapters, inventory, doctor, policy, apply, or verification implementation.
data.decision: Do not connect to the real NUC until the equivalent read-only chain is green in the disposable lab; production mutation additionally requires plan, approval or policy, bounded apply, readback verify, and monitoring.
consequences: The real NUC is a later explicit trust-boundary transition, initially read-only; lab shortcuts may not weaken production safety.
